title: Out-of-Order Scoreboard 2-Entry Reservation Station
description:
### Problem statement
Out-of-order superscalar execution engines track pending operand dependencies via Reservation Stations (Tomasulo algorithm). When an instruction dispatches, it reserves an entry, storing source operand values or physical register broadcast tags ($Q_j, Q_k$).

Design a 2-entry reservation station slice for ALU operations:
- Entry has fields: `busy`, `op[1:0]`, `vj[7:0]`, `qj[1:0]` (0 if ready, non-zero tag if pending), `vk[7:0]`, `qk[1:0]`.
- When `dispatch = 1` and entry is free:
  - Loads opcode `disp_op`, source tags/values.
- Snooping Common Data Bus (CDB): when `cdb_valid = 1` with tag `cdb_tag[1:0]` and data `cdb_data[7:0]`:
  - If `qj == cdb_tag`, latch `vj <= cdb_data`, `qj <= 0`.
  - If `qk == cdb_tag`, latch `vk <= cdb_data`, `qk <= 0`.
- Issue logic: an entry is ready to issue when `busy && (qj == 0) && (qk == 0)`.
- When entry issues (`issue_ack = 1`), `busy` clears and `issue_valid = 1`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_reservation_station(
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        disp_valid,
    input  wire [1:0]  disp_op,
    input  wire [7:0]  disp_vj,
    input  wire [1:0]  disp_qj,
    input  wire [7:0]  disp_vk,
    input  wire [1:0]  disp_qk,
    input  wire        cdb_valid,
    input  wire [1:0]  cdb_tag,
    input  wire [7:0]  cdb_data,
    input  wire        issue_ack,
    output reg         station_busy,
    output wire        issue_ready,
    output reg  [1:0]  issue_op,
    output reg  [7:0]  issue_vj,
    output reg  [7:0]  issue_vk
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all registers reset to 0.

    input  wire        clk,

Compare cdb_tag against qj and qk on cdb_valid.

title: Network-on-Chip (NoC) Virtual Channel Matrix Allocator
description:
### Problem statement
In Network-on-Chip routers, head flits allocate downstream Virtual Channels (VCs) to prevent wormhole routing deadlocks. Design a 2-requester to 2-VC separable matrix allocator.

Two input ports request downstream VCs (`req_0[1:0]`, `req_1[1:0]` where bit 0 is VC0, bit 1 is VC1). Each VC can only be allocated to ONE input port per cycle.

Arbitration rules:
- VC0 arbiter: Port 0 has priority if both request VC0.
- VC1 arbiter: Port 1 has priority if both request VC1.
- Each input port can only be granted at most ONE VC per cycle.
- Outputs: `grant_0[1:0]` (VC grant for Port 0), `grant_1[1:0]` (VC grant for Port 1).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_vc_allocator(
    input  wire [1:0] req_0,
    input  wire [1:0] req_1,
    output reg  [1:0] grant_0,
    output reg  [1:0] grant_1
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
- Grants are mutually exclusive per VC and per Port.
solution_hints: Evaluate VC0: grant to Port 0 if req_0[0], else to Port 1 if req_1[0].
Evaluate VC1: grant to Port 1 if req_1[1], else to Port 0 if req_0[1].
Ensure no single port receives both VC0 and VC1 grants simultaneously.

title: MSI Multi-Core Cache Coherence Protocol Snooping FSM
description:
### Problem statement
In shared-memory multi-core architectures, local L1 cache lines follow the classic MSI (Modified, Shared, Invalid) snooping protocol:
- State 0 (`2'b00`): **INVALID (I)**
- State 1 (`2'b01`): **SHARED (S)**
- State 2 (`2'b10`): **MODIFIED (M)**

State transitions occur on Local CPU requests (`pr_read`, `pr_write`) and Bus Snooping events (`bus_read`, `bus_write`):
- From **I**:
  - `pr_read`: transitions to **S**, generates `bus_rd_req = 1`.
  - `pr_write`: transitions to **M**, generates `bus_rdx_req = 1`.
- From **S**:
  - `pr_write`: transitions to **M**, generates `bus_inv_req = 1`.
  - `bus_write` (external snoop): transitions to **I**.
- From **M**:
  - `bus_read` (external snoop): transitions to **S**, asserts `writeback = 1`.
  - `bus_write` (external snoop): transitions to **I**, asserts `writeback = 1`.

Implement the single-cache-line MSI coherence controller.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_msi_coherence(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       pr_read,
    input  wire       pr_write,
    input  wire       bus_read,
    input  wire       bus_write,
    output reg  [1:0] cache_state,
    output reg        bus_rd_req,
    output reg        bus_rdx_req,
    output reg        bus_inv_req,
    output reg        writeback
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- Reset sets `cache_state <= 2'b00` (INVALID), all flags <= 0.

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       pr_read,
    input  wire       pr_write,
    input  wire       bus_read,
    input  wire       bus_write,
    output reg  [1:0] cache_state,
    output reg        bus_rd_req,
    output reg        bus_rdx_req,
    output reg        bus_inv_req,
    output reg        writeback
);
    // TODO: implement MSI snooping coherence controller

endmodule
solution_hints: Use a 3-state FSM encoding: 2'b00 (I), 2'b01 (S), 2'b10 (M).
Clear single-cycle output pulses (bus_rd_req, bus_rdx_req, etc.) on each cycle unless asserted.
In M state, both bus_read and bus_write trigger writeback.

title: AES-128 MixColumns 4-Byte Column Matrix Transformation
description:
### Problem statement
In AES-128, the `MixColumns` step treats each 4-byte column as a polynomial over $\text{GF}(2^8)$ and multiplies it modulo $x^4 + 1$ by fixed matrix:
$$\begin{bmatrix} s'_0 \\ s'_1 \\ s'_2 \\ s'_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} s_0 \\ s_1 \\ s_2 \\ s_3 \end{bmatrix}$$

In $\text{GF}(2^8)$:
- Multiply by 1: $1 \cdot s = s$.
- Multiply by 2 (`xtimes`): `xtimes(b) = b[7] ? ((b << 1) ^ 8'h1B) : (b << 1)`.
- Multiply by 3: $3 \cdot s = xtimes(s) \oplus s$.
- Addition is bitwise XOR ($\oplus$).

Implement the combinational MixColumns single column transformation for 4 input bytes `s0, s1, s2, s3` to produce `d0, d1, d2, d3`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_aes_mixcolumns(
    input  wire [7:0] s0,
    input  wire [7:0] s1,
    input  wire [7:0] s2,
    input  wire [7:0] s3,
    output wire [7:0] d0,
    output wire [7:0] d1,
    output wire [7:0] d2,
    output wire [7:0] d3
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_aes_mixcolumns(
    input  wire [7:0] s0,
    input  wire [7:0] s1,
    input  wire [7:0] s2,
    input  wire [7:0] s3,
    output wire [7:0] d0,
    output wire [7:0] d1,
    output wire [7:0] d2,
    output wire [7:0] d3
);
    // TODO: implement AES MixColumns single column transformation

endmodule
solution_hints: Implement function [7:0] xtime(input [7:0] b); xtime = b[7] ? ((b << 1) ^ 8'h1B) : (b << 1); endfunction.
d0 = xtime(s0) ^ (xtime(s1) ^ s1) ^ s2 ^ s3.
d1 = s0 ^ xtime(s1) ^ (xtime(s2) ^ s2) ^ s3; rotate terms symmetrically.

title: Fix: Dual-Core Lockstep Safety Divergence Comparator Bug
description:
### Problem statement
ISO 26262 ASIL-D automotive safety MCUs run two identical processor cores in cycle-accurate lockstep with a 2-cycle delay on the shadow core to prevent common-cause power transients from affecting both cores identically.

A comparator compared Core 0 outputs against Core 1 outputs immediately without delaying Core 0's signals by 2 cycles, triggering permanent false divergence alarms.

Fix the lockstep comparator:
- Delay `core0_data[7:0]` and `core0_valid` through a 2-stage shift register (`pipe1, pipe2`).
- On each clock cycle:
  - Compare delayed `core0_data` against `core1_data[7:0]` when delayed `core0_valid` is 1.
  - If mismatch occurs: `divergence_alarm` asserts and latches.
  - Count mismatch events `mismatch_count[2:0]`.
- Reset clears `divergence_alarm <= 0, mismatch_count <= 0`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_lockstep_fix(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       core0_valid,
    input  wire [7:0] core0_data,
    input  wire       core1_valid,
    input  wire [7:0] core1_data,
    input  wire       clear_alarm,
    output reg        divergence_alarm,
    output reg  [2:0] mismatch_count
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_lockstep_fix(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       core0_valid,
    input  wire [7:0] core0_data,
    input  wire       core1_valid,
    input  wire [7:0] core1_data,
    input  wire       clear_alarm,
    output reg        divergence_alarm,
    output reg  [2:0] mismatch_count
);
    // BUGGY: immediate comparison without 2-cycle pipeline alignment

endmodule
solution_hints: Instantiate 2 pipeline stages for core0_valid and core0_data.
Compare stage2 valid/data against current core1_valid/data.
Mismatch triggers if both are valid and data differs, or if valids differ.

title: Fix: Floating-Point Flush-to-Zero (FTZ) Denormal Exponent Hazard
description:
### Problem statement
In real-time DSP audio processing, denormalized floating-point numbers ($E = 0$ with non-zero mantissa) incur massive pipeline penalties. Flush-to-Zero (FTZ) mode forces any input or output with $E = 0$ and $M \ne 0$ to true zero ($E = 0, M = 0$).

A buggy FTZ unit checked `mant_in == 0` instead of `exp_in == 0`, failing to flush denormals and corrupting normalized numbers that happened to have mantissa 0 (such as exact powers of 2).

Fix the FTZ module:
- If `ftz_en && (exp_in == 4'd0) && (mant_in != 8'd0)`:
  - Denormal detected: `exp_out = 4'd0`, `mant_out = 8'd0`, `denormal_flushed = 1`.
- Otherwise:
  - Pass through: `exp_out = exp_in`, `mant_out = mant_in`, `denormal_flushed = 0`.
- Sign bit `sign_out = sign_in` in all cases.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_ftz_fix(
    input  wire       ftz_en,
    input  wire       sign_in,
    input  wire [3:0] exp_in,
    input  wire [7:0] mant_in,
    output wire       sign_out,
    output reg  [3:0] exp_out,
    output reg  [7:0] mant_out,
    output reg        denormal_flushed
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_ftz_fix(
    input  wire       ftz_en,
    input  wire       sign_in,
    input  wire [3:0] exp_in,
    input  wire [7:0] mant_in,
    output wire       sign_out,
    output reg  [3:0] exp_out,
    output reg  [7:0] mant_out,
    output reg        denormal_flushed
);
    // BUGGY: incorrect denormal check

endmodule
solution_hints: assign sign_out = sign_in.
Condition is: ftz_en && (exp_in == 4'd0) && (mant_in != 8'd0).
When condition holds, zero out mant_out and assert denormal_flushed.

title: Implement the timing: PCI Express 3-DW Header Packet Framer
description:
### Problem statement
PCI Express Transaction Layer Packets (TLPs) transmit 32-bit Dwords (DW) across consecutive clock cycles: Start of Packet (STP), Header DW0, Header DW1, Header DW2, followed by End of Packet (END).

Implement the 4-cycle TLP header transmission timing generator:
- On `start_tlp = 1`:
  - Cycle 0: `tlp_valid = 1, tlp_phase = 2'b00` (Header DW0: Format/Type).
  - Cycle 1: `tlp_valid = 1, tlp_phase = 2'b01` (Header DW1: Requester ID / Tag).
  - Cycle 2: `tlp_valid = 1, tlp_phase = 2'b10` (Header DW2: Memory Address).
  - Cycle 3: `tlp_valid = 1, tlp_phase = 2'b11, tlp_end = 1` (TLP End framing).
- Cycle 4: Return to IDLE (`tlp_valid = 0, tlp_end = 0`).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_pcie_tlp_timing(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       start_tlp,
    output reg        tlp_valid,
    output reg  [1:0] tlp_phase,
    output reg        tlp_end,
    output reg        busy
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.

title: Implement the timing: AXI4 WRAP4 Cache-Line Burst Generator
description:
### Problem statement
AXI4 WRAP bursts are used for cache line fills: a 4-beat 4-byte wrap burst (16-byte total wrap boundary) begins at any 4-byte aligned start address $A$ and increments addresses by 4, wrapping around within the 16-byte boundary.

For example, if start address is `0x0C`:
- Beat 0: `addr = 0x0C`
- Beat 1: `addr = 0x00` (wrapped)
- Beat 2: `addr = 0x04`
- Beat 3: `addr = 0x08`, `wlast = 1`

Implement the WRAP4 burst generator:
- When `start_burst = 1`: load `start_addr[7:0]`, output Beat 0 address.
- On each `beat_ack = 1`: advance to next beat.
- Wrap boundary is aligned to 16 bytes: `addr[3:0]` wraps `4'hC -> 4'h0 -> 4'h4 -> 4'h8`, while `addr[7:4]` remains unchanged.
- On Beat 3: assert `wlast = 1`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_axi_wrap4_timing(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       start_burst,
    input  wire [7:0] start_addr,
    input  wire       beat_ack,
    output reg  [7:0] curr_addr,
    output reg        wlast,
    output reg        burst_active
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_axi_wrap4_timing(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       start_burst,
    input  wire [7:0] start_addr,
    input  wire       beat_ack,
    output reg  [7:0] curr_addr,
    output reg        wlast,
    output reg        burst_active
);
    // TODO: implement AXI4 WRAP4 burst address timing

endmodule
solution_hints: The upper bits curr_addr[7:4] remain constant throughout the 4 beats.
Lower bits curr_addr[3:2] increment modulo 4 (0->1->2->3->0).
Set wlast = 1 when beat count is 3.

title: Checker: AXI-Stream Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) Oversize Guard
description:
### Problem statement
Network interface controllers enforce a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU). If an incoming AXI-Stream packet contains more than `MAX_BEATS = 4` beats before `TLAST` is observed, an MTU violation occurs.

Implement the MTU monitor:
- On each `tvalid && tready` beat, increment `pkt_beats`.
- If `pkt_beats > 4` and packet has not terminated (`!tlast`), `mtu_violation` asserts and latches.
- When `tvalid && tready && tlast`: packet terminates, `pkt_beats` resets to 0.
- Reset or `clear_err` clears `mtu_violation`.
- Counter `violation_count[2:0]` increments on each violation event.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_axis_mtu_chk(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       tvalid,
    input  wire       tready,
    input  wire       tlast,
    input  wire       clear_err,
    output reg        mtu_violation,
    output reg  [2:0] violation_count
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_axis_mtu_chk(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       tvalid,
    input  wire       tready,
    input  wire       tlast,
    input  wire       clear_err,
    output reg        mtu_violation,
    output reg  [2:0] violation_count

    // TODO: implement AXI-Stream MTU packet length checker

endmodule

If counter reaches 4 on an ongoing packet without tlast, trigger mtu_violation on 5th beat.
Hold mtu_violation until clear_err.

title: Checker: Multi-Core Ticket Lock Protocol & Reentrancy Guard
description:
### Problem statement
Ticket locks provide fair FIFO mutual exclusion among cores: a core requests a ticket (`fetch_and_add`), and when `now_serving == my_ticket`, the lock is granted. When releasing the lock, `now_serving` increments.

Two fatal safety violations can occur:
1. **Spurious Release**: Core releases lock when it is not holding it (`release && (now_serving != held_ticket)`).
2. **Double Acquire**: Core requests a ticket when it already holds an active ticket without releasing first.

Design the ticket lock checker for a single observing core:
- If spurious release occurs: `protocol_violation` asserts and latches.
- If double acquire occurs: `protocol_violation` asserts and latches.
- `lock_held` indicates whether the core currently holds the critical section.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_ticket_lock_chk(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       req_ticket,
    input  wire [3:0] ticket_assigned,
    input  wire [3:0] now_serving,
    input  wire       release_lock,
    input  wire       clear_err,
    output reg        lock_held,
    output reg        protocol_violation
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_ticket_lock_chk(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       req_ticket,
    input  wire [3:0] ticket_assigned,
    input  wire [3:0] now_serving,
    input  wire       release_lock,
    input  wire       clear_err,
    output reg        lock_held,
    output reg        protocol_violation
);
    // TODO: implement ticket lock protocol checker

endmodule
solution_hints: Maintain internal state: has_ticket, my_ticket.
Assert lock_held when has_ticket && (now_serving == my_ticket).
Trigger protocol_violation if release_lock arrives when !lock_held, or req_ticket when has_ticket.

title: Direct-Mapped Cache Controller with Dirty Line Writeback FSM
description:
### Problem statement
A direct-mapped 4-line L1 data cache tracks `valid`, `dirty`, and `tag[1:0]` for each line. When CPU requests a memory write (`cpu_req && is_write`) to address `addr[3:0]` (index `addr[1:0]`, tag `addr[3:2]`):
- **Hit**: if line is `valid && (line_tag == tag)`:
  - Write completes in 1 cycle, set `line_dirty <= 1, cpu_ack <= 1`.
- **Miss (Clean)**: if line is `!valid` or `!line_dirty`:
  - Fetch new line from RAM (`mem_read = 1`), update tag, write data, set `line_dirty <= 1, cpu_ack <= 1`.
- **Miss (Dirty)**: if line is `valid && line_dirty && (line_tag != tag)`:
  - Evict old line to RAM first (`mem_write = 1` for 1 cycle), then fetch new line (`mem_read = 1`), then set `cpu_ack <= 1`.

Implement the cache controller FSM.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_cache_writeback(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       cpu_req,
    input  wire [3:0] addr,
    input  wire       mem_ack,
    output reg        cpu_ack,
    output reg        mem_read,
    output reg        mem_write,
    output reg        busy
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all cache lines invalid, outputs reset to 0.

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,

FSM states: IDLE, WRITE_BACK, FETCH.
Assert cpu_ack immediately on cache hit or after fetching finishes.

title: 4x4 Pipelined Carry-Save Array (CSA) Multiplier
description:
### Problem statement
Carry-Save Array (CSA) multipliers eliminate ripple-carry propagation within the partial product reduction tree by representing intermediate sums as independent sum ($S$) and carry ($C$) vectors.

Implement the 4x4 unsigned multiplier using Carry-Save Addition:
- Inputs: `a[3:0]`, `b[3:0]`.
- Pipelined across 2 cycles:
  - Stage 1: Partial product generation and 4-row carry-save reduction producing final sum vector `sum_vec[7:0]` and carry vector `carry_vec[7:0]`.
  - Stage 2: Final vector addition `prod[7:0] = sum_vec + carry_vec`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_csa_multiplier(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       enable,
    input  wire [3:0] a,
    input  wire [3:0] b,
    output reg  [7:0] prod,
    output reg        valid_out
);
```

#### Specifications
- 2-stage synchronous pipeline.
- On reset: `prod <= 8'd0, valid_out <= 1'b0`.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_csa_multiplier(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       enable,
    input  wire [3:0] a,
    input  wire [3:0] b,
    output reg  [7:0] prod,
    output reg        valid_out
);
    // TODO: implement 2-stage carry-save array multiplier

endmodule
solution_hints: Stage 1 calculates the 8-bit product combinatorially and registers intermediate result.
Stage 2 registers final product to prod and propagates valid_out.
Ensure valid_out follows enable through the 2 pipeline registers.

title: Scatter-Gather DMA Linked-List Descriptor Fetch FSM
description:
### Problem statement
Scatter-Gather DMA engines traverse linked lists of memory descriptors stored in RAM. Each descriptor contains `{src_addr[7:0], dst_addr[7:0], len[3:0], next_ptr[7:0], is_last}`.

Implement the descriptor walker FSM:
- When `start_dma = 1` with initial descriptor address `head_ptr[7:0]`:
  - Step 1: Issue descriptor read `desc_read_req = 1` at `read_addr = curr_ptr`.
  - Step 2: When `desc_data_valid = 1`, latch `next_ptr` and `is_last`.
  - Step 3: Run data transfer (simulated with `transfer_active = 1` for 2 cycles).
  - Step 4: If `!is_last`, advance `curr_ptr <= next_ptr` and repeat from Step 1.
  - Step 5: If `is_last`, assert `dma_complete = 1`, return to IDLE.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_sg_dma_fsm(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       start_dma,
    input  wire [7:0] head_ptr,
    output reg        desc_read_req,
    output reg  [7:0] read_addr,
    input  wire       desc_data_valid,
    input  wire [7:0] desc_next_ptr,
    input  wire       desc_is_last,
    output reg        transfer_active,
```

title: AXI4 Out-of-Order Read Channel Reorder Buffer (ROB)
description:
### Problem statement
AXI4 permits out-of-order read data returns for different transaction IDs (`ARID`). To present in-order data to a processor core, a 2-entry Reorder Buffer (ROB) resequences out-of-order responses.

- When Entry $K$ receives its data, its `data_ready` flag is set.
- Retirement logic: Entry 0 must retire first (`commit_valid = 1`). Entry 1 can only retire after Entry 0 has retired.

Implement the 2-entry read reorder buffer.

```verilog
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       rvalid,
    input  wire       rid,
    input  wire [7:0] rdata,
    input  wire       commit_ack,
    output reg        commit_valid,

);
```

- On reset: all registers reset to 0.

title: Fix: Branch Target Buffer (BTB) Tag Aliasing Corruption Bug
description:
### Problem statement
A 4-entry Branch Target Buffer (BTB) predicted branches using only 2 bits of program counter (`pc[1:0]`) without checking the branch tag (`pc[7:2]`). Multiple distinct branch instructions mapped to the same index and aliased, predicting wild branch target jumps.

Fix the BTB:
- 4 entries indexed by `pc[1:0]`.
- Each entry stores `valid`, `tag[5:0] = pc[7:2]`, and `target[7:0]`.
- Prediction lookup (`predict = 1`):
  - If `valid && (tag == pc[7:2])`: `hit = 1, pred_target = target`.
  - Else: `hit = 0, pred_target = pc + 8'd2`.
- Update on branch resolution (`update = 1`):
  - Write `valid <= 1`, `tag <= update_pc[7:2]`, `target <= update_target` at index `update_pc[1:0]`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_btb_alias_fix(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       predict_req,
    input  wire [7:0] pc,
    input  wire       update_req,
    input  wire [7:0] update_pc,
    input  wire [7:0] update_target,
    output reg        hit,
    output reg  [7:0] pred_target
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all 4 entries invalid, outputs reset to 0.
starter_code:
module rtl_i_btb_alias_fix(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       predict_req,
    input  wire [7:0] pc,
    input  wire       update_req,
    input  wire [7:0] update_pc,
    input  wire [7:0] update_target,
    output reg        hit,
    output reg  [7:0] pred_target
);
    // BUGGY: no tag checking, causing aliasing corruption

endmodule
solution_hints: Maintain btb_valid[0..3], btb_tag[0..3], btb_target[0..3].
On predict_req, check btb_valid[pc[1:0]] && (btb_tag[pc[1:0]] == pc[7:2]).
Default pred_target on miss is pc + 8'd2.

title: Fix: Open-Drain Serial Bus Passive Pullup Decay Bug
description:
### Problem statement
In I2C and SMBus open-drain communication, devices actively pull lines low (`drive_low = 1`), relying on external passive pull-up resistors to return lines to logic 1 (`drive_low = 0`). A buggy accelerator drove active push-pull high (`1'b1`), destroying bus multi-master arbitration and causing short circuits when peer nodes pulled low.

Fix the open-drain driver model:
- Line output enable `line_oe = drive_low`.
- Output data pin `line_dout = 1'b0` (always ground when enabled).
- When `drive_low = 0`, line is tri-stated (`line_oe = 0`).
- Model an internal bus monitor: if `line_oe && line_din`, a bus contention conflict has occurred (`contention_fault <= 1`).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_opendrain_fix(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire drive_low,
    input  wire line_din,
    input  wire clear_fault,
    output wire line_oe,
    output wire line_dout,
    output reg  contention_fault
);
```

#### Specifications
- `line_oe = drive_low`, `line_dout = 1'b0`.
- Synchronous registered `contention_fault`.
- On reset: `contention_fault <= 0`.

    input  wire rst_n,

    input  wire line_din,

    output wire line_dout,
    output reg  contention_fault

    // BUGGY: drives active push-pull high

endmodule

Detect fault if drive_low && line_din (pulling low but line remains high).

title: Implement the timing: SDRAM Burst Read Interrupted by Precharge
description:
### Problem statement
In SDRAM, an ongoing read burst of length 4 can be prematurely terminated by issuing a `PRECHARGE` command. The command terminates the read burst and trunctuates the pipeline.

Implement the burst interruption sequencer:
- Cycle 0: `start_burst = 1` issues `READ` command (`cmd = 3'b101`, `busy = 1`).
- Cycle 1: NOP (`cmd = 3'b111`).
- Cycle 2: `data_valid = 1` (Beat 0 of read data).
- If `interrupt_precharge = 1` pulses at Cycle 2:
  - Cycle 3: `cmd = 3'b010` (PRE command), `data_valid = 1` (Beat 1, last beat allowed).
  - Cycle 4: NOP (`cmd = 3'b111`), `data_valid = 0` (Beats 2 and 3 truncated).
  - Cycle 5: NOP (`cmd = 3'b111`), `busy = 0` (Sequence complete).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_sdram_burst_interrupt(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       start_burst,
    input  wire       interrupt_precharge,
    output reg  [2:0] cmd,
    output reg        data_valid,
    output reg        busy
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- Commands: READ = `3'b101`, PRE = `3'b010`, NOP = `3'b111`.
- On reset: `cmd <= 3'b111, data_valid <= 0, busy <= 0`.

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       start_burst,
    input  wire       interrupt_precharge,

    output reg        data_valid,
    output reg        busy
);

endmodule

Latching interrupt_precharge forces early transition to precharge cycle.

title: Checker: AXI Write Response Channel BRESP Protocol Monitor
description:

In AXI4, write transactions must return `BVALID && BREADY` responses. A write response must NEVER be returned for an ID that was not previously addressed by `AWVALID && AWREADY`.

```verilog
    output reg  [2:0] brownout_counter

```

title: Radix-2 Non-Restoring Integer Divider Elementary Step
description:
### Problem statement
Non-restoring division avoids trial addition/restoration steps by using signed partial remainders. In Radix-2 non-restoring division, at step $i$:
- If partial remainder $R_{i-1} \ge 0$:
  - $R_i = (R_{i-1} \ll 1) - D$
  - $q_i = 1$
- If partial remainder $R_{i-1} < 0$:
  - $R_i = (R_{i-1} \ll 1) + D$
  - $q_i = 0$

Implement the combinational single-step Radix-2 non-restoring divider cell:
- Inputs: signed 8-bit partial remainder `r_in[7:0]`, signed 8-bit divisor `d_in[7:0]`.
- Shift left 1 bit: `shifted = {r_in[6:0], 1'b0}`.
- Outputs: `r_out[7:0]`, `q_bit` (1 if r_in >= 0, else 0).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_nonrestoring_step(
    input  wire [7:0] r_in,
    input  wire [7:0] d_in,
    output wire [7:0] r_out,
    output wire       q_bit
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
- Math is signed two's complement modulo 256 arithmetic.
solution_hints: Check r_in sign bit: wire sign_r = r_in[7].
assign q_bit = ~sign_r.
assign r_out = ~sign_r ? ({r_in[6:0], 1'b0} - d_in) : ({r_in[6:0], 1'b0} + d_in).

title: Floating-Point Leading Zero Anticipator (LZA) Normalizer
description:
### Problem statement
Floating-point subtractors suffer from massive cancellation: when subtracting two nearly equal significands, leading zeros appear that must be counted to normalize the mantissa.

Implement the 8-bit Leading Zero Counter (LZC):
- Input: `mant_in[7:0]`.
- Outputs: `lz_count[2:0]` (number of leading zeros, 0..7), `is_zero` (1 if `mant_in == 0`), and `normalized_mant[7:0]` shifted left by `lz_count`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_lza_normalizer(
    input  wire [7:0] mant_in,
    output reg  [2:0] lz_count,
    output wire       is_zero,
    output wire [7:0] normalized_mant
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
- `is_zero = (mant_in == 8'd0)`.
- `normalized_mant = mant_in << lz_count`.
solution_hints: Use priority encoder logic: if (mant_in[7]) lz_count = 0; else if (mant_in[6]) lz_count = 1; etc.
assign is_zero = (mant_in == 8'd0).
assign normalized_mant = mant_in << lz_count.

title: Dual-Issue Superscalar Execution Bypass Crossbar Matrix
description:
### Problem statement
In a 2-way superscalar processor, Instruction 1 in the same issue group can depend on the result of Instruction 0 (intra-group dependency), or either instruction can depend on results from the prior EX/MEM cycle.

Design the dual-ALU bypass multiplexer:
- Source operand `rs_addr[1:0]` with architectural data `rf_val[7:0]`.
- Prior ALU0 result: `alu0_val[7:0]` (dest `alu0_rd[1:0]`, valid `alu0_we`).
- Prior ALU1 result: `alu1_val[7:0]` (dest `alu1_rd[1:0]`, valid `alu1_we`).
- Forwarding priority: ALU1 (younger) > ALU0 (older) > Register File.
- If `rs_addr == 0`: always return 8'd0.
- Output bypassed operand `op_out[7:0]`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_dual_forward(
    input  wire [1:0] rs_addr,
    input  wire [7:0] rf_val,
    input  wire       alu0_we,
    input  wire [1:0] alu0_rd,
    input  wire [7:0] alu0_val,
    input  wire       alu1_we,
    input  wire [1:0] alu1_rd,
    input  wire [7:0] alu1_val,
    output reg  [7:0] op_out
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.

    input  wire [1:0] rs_addr,
    input  wire [7:0] rf_val,
    input  wire       alu0_we,

    input  wire [7:0] alu0_val,
    input  wire       alu1_we,
    input  wire [1:0] alu1_rd,

Next check younger ALU1: alu1_we && (alu1_rd != 0) && (alu1_rd == rs_addr).
Next check older ALU0, and fall back to rf_val.

title: 3-Stage MTBF-Hardened Clock Domain Crossing Synchronizer
description:
### Problem statement
In ultra-deep submicron FinFET nodes, mean time between failures (MTBF) requires 3-stage flip-flop synchronizers for asynchronous single-bit control signals. In addition, an edge detector detects both rising and falling edges of the synchronized signal.

Implement the 3-flop synchronizer with edge flags:
- Pipeline registers: `s1 <= async_in`, `s2 <= s1`, `s3 <= s2`.
- Output synchronized signal: `sync_out = s3`.
- Detect edges on synchronized domain: `rise_edge = s3 && !s3_d`, `fall_edge = !s3 && s3_d` where `s3_d` is `s3` delayed by 1 clock cycle.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_mtbf_sync(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire async_in,
    output reg  sync_out,
    output wire rise_edge,
    output wire fall_edge
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all synchronizer registers and delayed registers reset to 0.
solution_hints: Maintain s1, s2, s3 (which is sync_out), and s3_d.
rise_edge = sync_out && !s3_d.
fall_edge = !sync_out && s3_d.

title: Fix: Store Buffer Partial Byte Merge Read Forwarding Bug
description:
### Problem statement
Store buffers queue pending stores until retirement. When a load reads from memory, it snoops the store buffer to forward bytes. If a prior store only wrote 1 byte (`byte_mask = 2'b01`) of a 2-byte halfword, the buggy design forwarded all 16 bits of the store buffer, corrupting the unmodified byte.

Fix the store forwarding unit for a 16-bit word (2 bytes: byte 1 `[15:8]`, byte 0 `[7:0]`):
- Memory read returns `mem_rdata[15:0]`.
- Store buffer has pending store at matching address with `sb_data[15:0]` and `sb_mask[1:0]`.
- Forwarded result:
  - Byte 0: `sb_mask[0] ? sb_data[7:0] : mem_rdata[7:0]`.
  - Byte 1: `sb_mask[1] ? sb_data[15:8] : mem_rdata[15:8]`.
- Signal `partial_forward = (sb_mask == 2'b01 || sb_mask == 2'b10)`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_store_forward_fix(
    input  wire [15:0] mem_rdata,
    input  wire        sb_match,
    input  wire [15:0] sb_data,
    input  wire [1:0]  sb_mask,
    output wire [15:0] merged_rdata,
    output wire        partial_forward
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
- If `!sb_match`: `merged_rdata = mem_rdata`, `partial_forward = 0`.
solution_hints: Byte 0: (sb_match && sb_mask[0]) ? sb_data[7:0] : mem_rdata[7:0].
Byte 1: (sb_match && sb_mask[1]) ? sb_data[15:8] : mem_rdata[15:8].
partial_forward = sb_match && (sb_mask == 2'b01 || sb_mask == 2'b10).

title: Fix: Pipelined Integer Divider Zero-Divisor Trap Assertion
description:
### Problem statement
A pipelined divider takes 3 cycles to compute results. When a divide-by-zero (`divisor == 0`) occurred, the exception flag was asserted immediately at cycle 0 while the quotient output appeared at cycle 3, desynchronizing the exception from the architectural instruction retirement.

Fix the exception pipeline:
- Propagate `div_by_zero` exception flag through a 3-stage shift register matching the datapath pipeline depth.
- At cycle 3 when `valid_out = 1`:

  - Else: output computed quotient and `div_by_zero_trap = 0`.

#### Module interface
```verilog

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       valid_in,
    input  wire [7:0] dividend,
    input  wire [3:0] divisor,
    output reg        valid_out,
    output reg  [7:0] quot_out,
    output reg        div_by_zero_trap
);
```

#### Specifications
- Exactly 3 clock cycles of latency from `valid_in` to `valid_out`.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       valid_in,

    output reg  [7:0] quot_out,

Pipeline zero-divisor detection (divisor == 0) across 3 registers: z1, z2, div_by_zero_trap.
Compute quotient and pipe through matching delay registers.

title: Implement the timing: DDR3 Memory Write Leveling Calibration FSM
description:
### Problem statement
DDR3 uses a fly-by topology with write leveling to deskew clock `CK` and data strobe `DQS` delays to individual SDRAM chips.

- Enter write leveling mode when `start_leveling = 1`.

  - Step 2: Read back DQ sampling feedback `dq_feedback` (0 if DQS arrived before CK, 1 if DQS aligned/past CK).

  - If `dq_feedback == 0`: increment `step_count`, repeat.

#### Module interface
```verilog

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       start_leveling,
    input  wire       dq_feedback,
    output reg        dqs_pulse,
    output reg  [1:0] delay_lock,
    output reg        leveling_done,
    output reg        busy
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,

    output reg  [1:0] delay_lock,

If dq_feedback is 1 on SAMPLE_DQ, lock in delay_lock and assert leveling_done.

title: Implement the timing: Quad Peripheral Interface (QPI) Burst Sequence
description:
### Problem statement
Quad Peripheral Interface (QPI) executes all phases—opcode, address, and data—over 4 parallel lines (`IO[3:0]`). A 1-byte opcode requires 2 nibbles (2 cycles), a 3-byte address requires 6 nibbles (6 cycles), followed by 2 dummy cycles and data streaming.

Implement the QPI read sequence:
- Cycle 0..1: `cs_n = 0, phase = 2'b00` (Opcode phase, 2 nibbles).
- Cycle 2..3: `cs_n = 0, phase = 2'b01` (Address phase slice, 2 nibbles).
- Cycle 4: `cs_n = 0, phase = 2'b10` (Dummy turnaround cycle).
- Cycle 5..6: `cs_n = 0, phase = 2'b11, data_valid = 1` (Active data beats).

title: Multi-Core Atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS) Memory Engine
description:
### Problem statement
Lock-free concurrency algorithms depend on atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS): atomically read memory address $A$; if $M[A] == \text{expected}$, write $\text{new\_val}$ and return success ($1$); else leave $M[A]$ unmodified and return failure ($0$).

Implement the 4-location 8-bit atomic CAS memory slice:
- On `cas_req = 1`:
  - Compare `mem[addr[1:0]]` with `expected_val[7:0]`.
  - If match: `mem[addr[1:0]] <= new_val[7:0]`, `cas_success <= 1`.
  - If mismatch: memory unchanged, `cas_success <= 0`.
  - In either case, return `prev_val <= mem[addr[1:0]]`.
- When `cas_req = 0`: hold values.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_atomic_cas(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       cas_req,
    input  wire [1:0] addr,
    input  wire [7:0] expected_val,
    input  wire [7:0] new_val,
    output reg        cas_success,
    output reg  [7:0] prev_val
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all memory locations initialized to 0, outputs reset to 0.

title: RSA/ECC Montgomery Modular Multiplication Elementary Step
description:
### Problem statement
Public-key accelerators (RSA, ECDSA) perform modular reduction using Montgomery multiplication without division. For each bit of multiplier $B$:
- $T = A_{acc} + (b_i \cdot X)$
- $q = T[0]$ (since modulus $M$ is odd)
- $A_{next} = (T + (q \cdot M)) \gg 1$

Implement the combinational Montgomery modular addition step:
- Inputs: accumulator `a_in[7:0]`, multiplicand `x_in[7:0]`, multiplier bit `b_bit`, odd modulus `m_in[7:0]`.
- Step 1: `t = a_in + (b_bit ? x_in : 8'd0)` (9 bits).
- Step 2: `q = t[0]`.
- Step 3: `sum = t + (q ? m_in : 8'd0)` (10 bits).
- Output: `a_out[7:0] = sum[8:1]` (shifted right 1 bit).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_montgomery_step(
    input  wire [7:0] a_in,
    input  wire [7:0] x_in,
    input  wire       b_bit,
    input  wire [7:0] m_in,
    output wire [7:0] a_out
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
solution_hints: wire [8:0] t = a_in + (b_bit ? x_in : 8'd0);
wire q = t[0];
wire [9:0] sum = t + (q ? m_in : 8'd0); assign a_out = sum[8:1];

  - After completing $W \times H = 8$ total beats, assert `transfer_done = 1`.

title: Hardware Feistel Block Cipher Round Transformation Slice
description:
### Problem statement
Feistel network ciphers split a 16-bit block into Left (`L[7:0]`) and Right (`R[7:0]`) halves. In each round:
- $L_{i+1} = R_i$
- $R_{i+1} = L_i \oplus F(R_i, K_i)$
where round function $F(R, K) = ((R \ll 1) | (R \gg 7)) \oplus K$ (circular rotate left 1, XOR round key).

Implement the combinational single-round Feistel slice:
- Inputs: `l_in[7:0]`, `r_in[7:0]`, `k_in[7:0]`.
- Outputs: `l_out[7:0]`, `r_out[7:0]`.

#### Module interface
```verilog

    input  wire [7:0] l_in,
    input  wire [7:0] r_in,
    input  wire [7:0] k_in,
    output wire [7:0] l_out,
    output wire [7:0] r_out
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
solution_hints: assign l_out = r_in;
wire [7:0] rot_r = {r_in[6:0], r_in[7]};
assign r_out = l_in ^ (rot_r ^ k_in);

title: Fix: Dual-Port Cache CPU-Write vs Bus-Invalidate Port Collision
description:
### Problem statement
In dual-ported cache tag arrays, if the CPU pipeline attempts to write a line (`cpu_tag_we`) at the exact same cycle that external bus snooping invalidates the line (`snoop_inv_req` at matching line index), a coherence collision occurs.

A buggy design allowed the CPU write to proceed, resurrecting a stale, invalidated line and corrupting multi-core coherence. By protocol, Bus Invalidate MUST strictly dominate and cancel CPU local writes.

Fix the tag array port arbiter:
- Index `idx[1:0]` (4 lines). Line valid array `tag_valid[0..3]`.
- If `snoop_inv_req`: line `idx` must ALWAYS be cleared: `tag_valid[idx] <= 0`.
- If `cpu_tag_we` occurs without `snoop_inv_req`: `tag_valid[idx] <= 1`.
- If both assert on same index: Invalidation wins (`tag_valid[idx] <= 0`), and `collision_suppressed` asserts.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_tag_collision_fix(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire [1:0] idx,
    input  wire       cpu_tag_we,
    input  wire       snoop_inv_req,
    output reg  [3:0] tag_valid,
    output reg        collision_suppressed
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: `tag_valid <= 4'b0000, collision_suppressed <= 0`.
starter_code:

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire [1:0] idx,
    input  wire       cpu_tag_we,
    input  wire       snoop_inv_req,
    output reg  [3:0] tag_valid,
    output reg        collision_suppressed
);
    // BUGGY: CPU write takes precedence over snoop invalidation

endmodule
solution_hints: Check condition: if (snoop_inv_req) tag_valid[idx] <= 0.
collision_suppressed <= cpu_tag_we && snoop_inv_req.
Only set tag_valid[idx] <= 1 if cpu_tag_we && !snoop_inv_req.

title: Fix: Signed Pipelined Multiplier MSB Sign-Extension Truncation
description:
### Problem statement
A 4-bit signed multiplier produced an 8-bit signed product. The designer performed unsigned multiplication `$unsigned(a) * $unsigned(b)` and manually sign-extended bit 7, which erroneously corrupted products of two negative numbers (e.g. `-2 * -3 = +6`, but bit 7 sign logic produced negative results).

Fix the signed multiplier:
- Inputs: 4-bit two's complement signed `a[3:0]`, `b[3:0]`.
- Pipelined across 1 register stage.
- Output: 8-bit true two's complement product `prod[7:0]`.

```verilog
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire [3:0] a,
    input  wire [3:0] b,
    output reg  [7:0] prod
);
```

- On reset: `prod <= 8'd0`.

Verify negative times negative produces positive.

- Output `is_locked = !unlock_trip`.

```verilog
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire [3:0] phase_err,
```

- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.

title: Checker: Multi-Core Memory Barrier (FENCE) Ordering Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
In weakly-ordered memory models (e.g. RISC-V, ARM), a memory barrier instruction (`FENCE`) prevents younger memory requests from executing until all older pending memory requests have completed and drained from the write buffer (`pending_writes == 0`).

If a younger memory request (`younger_req = 1`) executes while a `fence_active` is asserted and older writes remain (`pending_writes > 0`), a catastrophic barrier ordering violation occurs.

Implement the memory barrier ordering checker:
- When `fence_cmd` asserts: set `fence_active <= 1`.
- When `pending_writes == 0`: clear `fence_active <= 0`.
- If `younger_req && fence_active && (pending_writes > 0)`: assert `barrier_violation` and latch until `clear_err`.

#### Module interface
```verilog

    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       fence_cmd,
    input  wire [2:0] pending_writes,
    input  wire       younger_req,
    input  wire       clear_err,
    output reg        fence_active,
    output reg        barrier_violation
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.

title: Hardware Multi-Core Mutex Semaphore Lock Engine
description:
### Problem statement
Hardware semaphores provide sub-nanosecond mutual exclusion across multiple CPU cores without operating system kernel traps.

Implement the 2-core hardware mutex engine:
- Inputs: `lock_req_0`, `unlock_req_0`, `lock_req_1`, `unlock_req_1`.
- Outputs: `granted_core[1:0]` (bit 0 for Core 0, bit 1 for Core 1), `is_locked`.
- Rules:
  - In unlocked state (`is_locked == 0`), if both cores request simultaneously, Core 0 wins priority.
  - While locked by Core $K$, the lock can only be released by `unlock_req` from Core $K$. Unlock requests from the other core are ignored.
  - When released, if the other core is waiting (`lock_req`), ownership immediately transfers to that core.

#### Module interface

```verilog
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire lock_req_0,
    input  wire unlock_req_0,
    input  wire lock_req_1,
    input  wire unlock_req_1,
    output reg  [1:0] granted_core,
    output wire is_locked
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- `is_locked = (granted_core != 2'b00)`.
- On reset: `granted_core <= 2'b00`.

title: 8b/10b Running Disparity (RD) Tracking & Inversion Engine
description:
### Problem statement
8b/10b line coding maintains DC balance by tracking Running Disparity ($RD \in \{-1, +1\}$). For each 10-bit symbol with $N_1$ ones and $N_0$ zeros:
- Disparity $\Delta = N_1 - N_0$.
- Next running disparity: $RD_{next} = RD + \Delta$.
- In standard 8b/10b, valid symbols have $\Delta \in \{-2, 0, +2\}$.

Implement the running disparity tracker:
- Represent $RD$: `0` for $RD = -1$, `1` for $RD = +1$.
- For each 10-bit input symbol `sym_in[9:0]` on `sym_valid = 1`:
  - Count number of ones ($N_1$).
  - If $N_1 > 5$ ($+2$ disparity): $RD_{next} = 1$.
  - If $N_1 < 5$ ($-2$ disparity): $RD_{next} = 0$.
  - If $N_1 == 5$ ($0$ disparity): $RD_{next} = RD$ (unchanged).
  - If $N_1 \notin \{4, 5, 6\}$, assert `illegal_disparity_err`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_rd_tracker(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       sym_valid,
    input  wire [9:0] sym_in,
    output reg        current_rd,
    output reg        illegal_disparity_err
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: `current_rd <= 0` (RD = -1), `illegal_disparity_err <= 0`.
solution_hints: Count ones using addition of bits: ones = sym_in[0] + sym_in[1] + ... + sym_in[9].
Update current_rd based on whether ones == 6 (rd=1) or ones == 4 (rd=0).
Flag illegal_disparity_err if ones < 4 or ones > 6.

title: Fused Multiply-Add (FMA) Product-Sum Exponent Alignment
description:
### Problem statement
In IEEE 754 Fused Multiply-Add ($A \times B + C$), the product exponent is $E_{prod} = E_A + E_B - \text{bias}$ (where bias = 7 for 4-bit exponents). To add addend $C$, the exponent difference between product and addend determines the shift alignment: $\Delta E = E_{prod} - E_C$.

Implement the FMA exponent alignment slice:
- Inputs: 4-bit exponents `ea[3:0]`, `eb[3:0]`, `ec[3:0]`.
- Bias = 7.
- Product exponent: `eprod = ea + eb - 4'd7`.
- If `eprod >= ec`: common exponent `e_common = eprod`, `shift_c = eprod - ec`, `shift_prod = 4'd0`.
- If `eprod < ec`: common exponent `e_common = ec`, `shift_prod = ec - eprod`, `shift_c = 4'd0`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_fma_exp_align(
    input  wire [3:0] ea,
    input  wire [3:0] eb,
    input  wire [3:0] ec,
    output wire [3:0] e_common,
    output wire [3:0] shift_prod,
    output wire [3:0] shift_c
);
```

#### Specifications
- Pure combinational logic.
solution_hints: wire [4:0] sum_ab = ea + eb;
wire [3:0] eprod = (sum_ab >= 5'd7) ? (sum_ab - 5'd7) : 4'd0;
Compare eprod with ec to determine e_common, shift_prod, and shift_c.

title: Fix: 2-Bit Saturating Branch Predictor State Counter Overflow Flaw
description:
### Problem statement
A 2-bit saturating branch predictor uses states `2'b00` (Strongly Not Taken), `2'b01` (Weakly Not Taken), `2'b10` (Weakly Taken), `2'b11` (Strongly Taken). A flawed counter implemented direct integer addition `state <= state + 1` and subtraction without saturating, wrapping `3 + 1 -> 0` and `0 - 1 -> 3` on consecutive taken/not-taken branches.

Fix the 2-bit saturating predictor:
- Predict: `pred_taken = state[1]` (MSB is 1 for Weakly/Strongly Taken).
- On `update_en = 1`:
  - If `actual_taken = 1`: increment unless `state == 2'b11` (clamps at 3).
  - If `actual_taken = 0`: decrement unless `state == 2'b00` (clamps at 0).
- On reset: `state <= 2'b01` (Weakly Not Taken).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_bht_sat_fix(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire update_en,
    input  wire actual_taken,
    output wire pred_taken,
    output reg  [1:0] state
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- `pred_taken = state[1]`.
solution_hints: assign pred_taken = state[1].
Clamp state at 2'b11 when actual_taken is 1.
Clamp state at 2'b00 when actual_taken is 0.

title: Fix: Arbiter Grant Combinational Ripple Glitch Hazard
description:
### Problem statement
A priority arbiter generated grant outputs purely combinatorially from asynchronous request lines: `grant[0] = req[0]; grant[1] = req[1] & ~req[0]`. When `req[0]` toggled, intermediate logic delays produced runt glitch pulses on `grant[1]`, causing slave devices to sample false bus accesses.

Fix the arbiter:
- Synchronize grants on the rising clock edge: `grant[1:0]` must be cleanly registered flip-flop outputs.
- Maintain 1-cycle minimum grant hold duration to eliminate intermediate runt pulses.
- When `req[0]` asserts, `grant <= 2'b01` on posedge clk.
- When `!req[0] && req[1]`, `grant <= 2'b10` on posedge clk.
- When no requests, `grant <= 2'b00`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_arbiter_glitch_fix(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire req_0,
    input  wire req_1,
    output reg  [1:0] grant
);
```

#### Specifications
- Fully synchronous registered outputs on posedge clk.
- On reset: `grant <= 2'b00`.
solution_hints: Register grant <= (req_0 ? 2'b01 : (req_1 ? 2'b10 : 2'b00)) on posedge clk.
Ensure synchronous reset clears grant to 0.
Eliminate all combinational assigns to grant.

title: Implement the timing: MIPI D-PHY High-Speed (HS) Entry Sequence
description:
### Problem statement
MIPI D-PHY high-speed serial links transition from Low-Power (LP) to High-Speed (HS) transmission through an exact state sequence:
- State 0: LP-11 (`dp=1, dn=1` - Stop State)
- State 1: LP-01 (`dp=0, dn=1` - HS-Request)
- State 2: LP-00 (`dp=0, dn=0` - HS-Prepare)
- State 3: HS-Zero (`hs_mode=1, dp=0, dn=0`)
- State 4: HS-Sync (`hs_mode=1, sync_leader=1`)

Implement the 4-cycle HS entry sequencer:
- In IDLE: `lp_state = 2'b11` (LP-11), `hs_mode = 0, sync_leader = 0`.
- When `hs_entry_req = 1`:
  - Cycle 0: `lp_state = 2'b01, hs_mode = 0`.
  - Cycle 1: `lp_state = 2'b00, hs_mode = 0`.
  - Cycle 2: `lp_state = 2'b00, hs_mode = 1, sync_leader = 0`.
  - Cycle 3: `lp_state = 2'b00, hs_mode = 1, sync_leader = 1` (HS Burst active).

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_mipi_dphy_timing(
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rst_n,
    input  wire       hs_entry_req,
    output reg  [1:0] lp_state,
    output reg        hs_mode,
    output reg        sync_leader
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: `lp_state <= 2'b11, hs_mode <= 0, sync_leader <= 0`.
solution_hints: Use a step counter running 0..3 triggered by hs_entry_req.
Map steps to {lp_state, hs_mode, sync_leader}.
Return to IDLE (lp_state = 2'b11) after completing step 3.

title: Implement the timing: Serial ATA Out-of-Band (OOB) Burst Generator
description:
### Problem statement
SATA Out-of-Band (OOB) signaling detects cable connection via repeated bursts of 1.5 GHz high-frequency pulses separated by quiet idle periods:
- A burst interval consists of 2 cycles of active signaling (`tx_burst = 1`), followed by 2 cycles of quiet line silence (`tx_burst = 0`).
- Generate a sequence of 2 complete OOB burst/quiet cycles (total 8 clock cycles).

Implement the SATA OOB burst generator:
- On `start_oob = 1`:
  - Cycles 0..1: `tx_burst = 1, oob_active = 1`.
  - Cycles 2..3: `tx_burst = 0, oob_active = 1`.
  - Cycles 4..5: `tx_burst = 1, oob_active = 1`.
  - Cycles 6..7: `tx_burst = 0, oob_active = 1`.
  - Cycle 8: Return to IDLE: `tx_burst = 0, oob_active = 0, oob_done = 1`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_sata_oob_timing(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire start_oob,
    output reg  tx_burst,
    output reg  oob_active,
    output reg  oob_done
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0.
solution_hints: Use a step counter running 0..7 when triggered by start_oob.
tx_burst is 1 when step is 0, 1, 4, 5.
Assert oob_done on cycle 8 and deassert oob_active.

title: Checker: DDR SDRAM Write-to-Read (tWTR) Turnaround Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
DDR memory devices require a minimum Write-to-Read turnaround delay ($t_{WTR} = 4$ clock cycles) between the final write burst data beat and issuing an internal `READ` command. If `read_cmd` asserts when less than 4 cycles have elapsed since `last_write_beat`, data bus contention will occur.

Implement the $t_{WTR}$ safety monitor:
- When `write_beat_last = 1`: reset turnaround counter `cycles_since_wr <= 0`.
- Increment `cycles_since_wr` each cycle until reaching saturated count 7.
- If `read_cmd && (cycles_since_wr < 4)`: assert `twtr_violation` and latch until `clear_err`.
- Counter `violation_count[2:0]` increments on each violation event.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_twtr_chk(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire write_beat_last,
    input  wire read_cmd,
    input  wire clear_err,
    output reg  twtr_violation,
    output reg  [2:0] violation_count
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- On reset: all outputs reset to 0, `cycles_since_wr` initializes to 7 (safe/idle).

title: Checker: Windowed Watchdog Timer (WWDT) Early-Kick Fault Guard
description:
### Problem statement
In ISO 26262 ASIL-D automotive systems, a Windowed Watchdog Timer (WWDT) detects runaway code loops: the watchdog service pulse (`kick_wdt`) must arrive within an allowable time window (`MIN_COUNT = 3 <= timer <= MAX_COUNT = 7`).

If `kick_wdt` is pulsed too early (`timer < 3`), an Early-Kick fault occurs. If `timer > 7`, an Expiration fault occurs. In either case, a catastrophic watchdog trip is triggered.

Implement the windowed watchdog safety guard:
- Internal `timer[3:0]` increments every clock cycle when enabled.
- On `kick_wdt`:
  - If `timer < 4'd3`: `early_fault` asserts and latches.
  - If `timer >= 4'd3 && timer <= 4'd7`: service is valid; `timer <= 0`.
- If `timer > 4'd7`: `expired_fault` asserts and latches.
- `system_trip = early_fault || expired_fault`.

#### Module interface
```verilog
module rtl_i_windowed_wdt_chk(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,
    input  wire kick_wdt,
    input  wire clear_trip,
    output wire system_trip,
    output reg  early_fault,
    output reg  expired_fault,
    output reg  [3:0] timer
);
```

#### Specifications
- Synchronous on posedge clk.
- `system_trip = early_fault || expired_fault`.
- On reset: all outputs and internal timer reset to 0.

    output reg  early_fault,

If kick_wdt arrives when timer < 3, trigger early_fault.
